notes.headline: Your master clips at +2.8 dBTP and sits at -2.68 LUFS — pull the limiter back and set a true-peak ceiling before anything else.
notes.summary: This is a solid-sounding master (7.8/10, 97% match to your reference) that's been pushed far past where it needs to go. True peak is +2.8 dBTP, above full scale, so it will distort on playback and again after MP3/AAC encoding, and at -2.68 LUFS integrated Spotify will turn it down about 11.3 dB anyway — you're paying in punch for loudness nobody hears. Back the limiter off and cap the ceiling, then look at the low end, which reads 4.4 dB lighter below 100 Hz than your reference at matched volume. Your stereo picture and balance are already in good shape, so this is mostly a gain-staging pass.

priorities.title: Over-limiting: peaks above full scale and no headroom left
priorities.why: At +2.8 dBTP the file is clipping converters and lossy encoders, and a peak-to-loudness ratio of 5.5 dB means the transients are already flattened. Since streaming turns -2.7 LUFS down by about 11.3 dB, the extra limiting only costs you punch — pulling it back is free dynamics.

priorities.title: Low end lighter than your reference
priorities.why: Below 100 Hz you're 4.4 dB under the reference at matched volume, so the master will feel thinner on systems with real low-end extension.

priorities.title: Little contrast between sections
priorities.why: Loudness range is 3.5 LU, so verses and choruses land at nearly the same level and the arrangement stops building. Easing the limiter will help, but section-level moves are what create the lift.

listen_for: After setting Pro Limiter's Ceiling to −1.0 dB with ISP on, listen to the loudest section for the grit and pumping that was there before — it should clean up.
With the limiter input down 2–4 dB, check kick and snare transients at matched volume; the hits should poke through rather than sit flat.
Loop the loudest section and A/B against your reference at matched volume while setting the low shelf, on whatever gives you honest sub — it's easy to overshoot 4.5 dB.
Play verse into chorus back to back and confirm the chorus actually feels like it arrives once the automation is in.
strengths: Stereo image is stable: L/R correlation 0.766 and low-end correlation 0.785, so the bottom stays centered.
Mono fold-down only costs 0.56 dB — nothing important is cancelling.
Left/right balance is dead center at 0.0 dB, and you match your reference 97% across loudness, punch, contrast, tone and width.

judge.priority_order: The critical true-peak/over-limiting group (F1,F3,F4) leads, followed by the warning-level low-end finding (F2), then the info-level LRA issue (F5), matching severity order.
judge.explains_impact: Each priority states real-world effect: distortion/converter clipping and lost punch for the first, thinner low end on systems with extension for F2, and stalled arrangement contrast for F5.
judge.groups_causes: F1, F3, and F4 are correctly merged as one over-limiting cause, while F2 (tonal) and F5 (section dynamics) are kept separate as distinct causes.
judge.specific: Notes cite exact figures like +2.8 dBTP, -2.68 LUFS, 4.4 dB below 100 Hz, 5.5 PLR, 3.5 LU, and the 97% reference match, all pulled from this report.
judge.stage_appropriate: Correctly treats this as a master and judges loudness/true-peak against release/streaming norms, consistent with the report's stage.
judge.faithful: The listen_for line about 'the grit and pumping that was there before — it should clean up' invents an audible artifact not stated anywhere in the report's measurements or findings.
judge.concise: The notes stay focused on the five findings with brief explanations and short listen-for/strengths lists, without padding or repetition.
